sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:13428  CRL.P No. 102918 of 2023  ORDER Heard Shri.Srinand A Pachhapure, learned counsel for the petitioner and Shri Praveena Y.
Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
2.

The petitioner is seeking anticipatory bail in Crime No. 64/2023 of Hotcholi Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420 r/w Section 149 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").
3. It is the case of the complainant that CEO of Taluk Panchayath, Shiraguppa lodged a complaint against the petitioner and others in respect of misappropriation of the amount under NAREGA Scheme.
The enquiry conducted by the Lokayuktha submitted their report on 14.01.2019.
As per the said report the amount of Rs.27,25,619/- said to have been misappropriated by the accused.
4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the offence is of the year 2015 and the report is of the year 2019.
However, the petitioner has been transferred to some other department in the year 2013.
It is further submitted that the overt act of this petitioner has not been NC: 2023:KHC-D:13428 attributed and the other accused have been discharged in this case.
The petitioner is the Assistant Executive Engineer working at National Highway, sub division-Chikkaballapur and he will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
The alleged offences are neither punishable with death nor imprisonment for life.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara, the learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the alleged offences are committed against the society at large.
The petitioner being the public servant misappropriated the amount sanctioned under the NAREGA Scheme.
The misappropriated amount is a huge amount.
Where financial restraints and constraints have taken place, the Court has to look after those matters seriously and therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss petition.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it NC: 2023:KHC-D:13428 is noticed that the petitioner was working as a Junior Engineer, Panchayathraj Engineering Sub-Division, Siruguppa, as on the date of the alleged incident.

It was Hatcholli Gram Panchayath Office, wherein the President and Secretary were also Sri. Rajareddy S/O Hanumantha Reddy vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169552565/
2 involved in this case

sentences.text: and they were arraigned as accused in the said scam.
However, they have been discharged by the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal.
Moreover, the alleged misappropriation said to have taken place in the year 2015 and the case has been registered on the strength of the report of the Lokayuktha.
Considering the avocation of the petitioner, it may be appropriated to grant anticipatory bail by imposing suitable conditions that would meet the apprehension of the prosecution.

7. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.64/2023 of Hatcholli Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409 and 420 of IPC R/w. 149 of IPC, by the respondent - Police, in the event of his arrest, on NC:
2023:KHC-D:13428 executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional police, subject to the following conditions:-
a) The petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station within one month from today.
On surrender, the jurisdictional police is directed to take the bond and surety on the same day.
b) The petitioner shall cooperate with the investigation, as and when it is required.
c) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
